newsitem.title: BELARUS: Clashes erupt at Belarus nationalist protest.
newsitem.headline: Clashes erupt at Belarus nationalist protest.

text.p: Scores of people battled with police in the Belarussian capital Minsk on Sunday when a nationalist protest against President Alexander Lukashenko erupted in clashes.

Police beat protesters with truncheons and nationalists fought back with their fists after about 4,000 demonstrators ignored a ban on marching and rallied on Yakob Kolas square. Fighting also broke out at a sanctioned rally, where a crowd of about 10,000 protesters had gathered.
Protesters attacked several police cars and shouted "Belarus into NATO" and "We will not sell our nation's glory". Several protesters appeared to have been injured.
The nationalists, who oppose Lukashenko's policy of forming a union with neighbouring Russia, were marking the anniversary of an independent republic created in 1918.

The republic lasted only a few months before being incorporated by Russian Bolsheviks. Many Belarussians are less than enthusiastic about the return of independence in 1991, favouring a new union with Moscow.

A loose union of prominent politicians, nationalists, intellectuals and students, mostly in the capital, oppose Lukashenko, who was awarded sweeping powers by most of the population of 10 million last November.
